exposure: Continuous skin-to-skin contact (SSC) in addition to routine rooming-in care
outcome: Newborn weight loss after birth (7% and 9% thresholds)
cohort: A total of 2205 women who delivered at Shanghai Changning District Maternal and Child Health Hospital between January and December 2022, and their newborns, were included in the study.
finding: Mother-infant rooming-in with continuous SSC promotes appropriate weight gain in newborns, increases breastfeeding rates, and reduces the need for jaundice medication compared to routine rooming-in care.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as a risk factor for excessive newborn weight loss (greater than 7%) and for the use of jaundice medication.
